_comment_controlled: The controlled roster under test. `value`/`checked`/`selected` are the generator's
DEFAULTS (kept identical here — and deliberately UNSCOPED — so the NB2c goldens hold
either way); `muted` and `pressed` exercise the config-driven half, and `reading`
exercises the ELEMENT SCOPE (NB2h).
`resyncs: false` is a fact about elm/virtual-dom, not a preference — its
controlled-input special-casing is keyed on the NAMES `value` and `checked` only,
so a `selected`/`muted` property whose model value has not changed is skipped
forever. The generated docs must say so.
`reading` is declared by wc-widget, wc-gauge AND wc-dial but scoped to wc-widget.
That is the shape of the native `value`, which seven elements declare at three IDL
types, and the three probe elements are the three cases:
- wc-widget — the <input>: a LIVE property that diverges from the content attribute
once the dirty-value flag is set. In scope.
- wc-gauge  — the <button>/<data>/<option>: a REFLECTED DOMString. Out of scope, so
it writes the content attribute, which reaches the property anyway and
also serializes. Still on the `reading` capability row, because a
string property write is harmless here.
- wc-dial   — the <progress>/<meter>/<li>: a NUMERIC IDL type. `Ir.property
"reading" (Json.Encode.string "abc")` against a `double` is a Web IDL
TypeError, thrown mid-patch, which kills the render loop rather than
one node. Scoping alone does NOT fix this, because the shared
Probe.Attributes.reading takes the PROPERTY form and every element
whose row carries the field admits it. So wc-dial LEAVES the row:
`_renames` gives it a different setter name and `attrTypes` the type
its value space actually has, and `A.reading` applied to a wc-dial is
then a COMPILE error instead of a runtime crash.
A separate name (rather than scoping `value` here) keeps NB2c pinning the unscoped
path at the same time.
_comment_variants: A variant over a SCOPED controlled base. It must follow its base's per-element form:
`Ir.property` + `Json.Encode.string` where the base is the live property (wc-widget,
and the shared Probe.Attributes), and a plain `Ir.attribute` where the base is a
content attribute (wc-gauge). The `Json.Encode.string`-never-`.float` rule is not a
style choice: virtual-dom compares property facts by identity against the previously
organized raw JS value, so a fact alternating between number and string under one
property name would make every diff a false positive.
It must ALSO be absent from wc-dial. `base` names a SETTER, not a DOM attribute, and
wc-dial renamed its `reading` away — its numeric value space already has the
correctly-typed `readingNumeric`, so a second Float setter there would be two names
for one fact, under a row `readingAsNumber` does not even claim.
_comment_renames: NB2i: wc-dial's `reading` value space is a NUMBER, so it must not share the `reading`
capability row with wc-widget and wc-gauge. `_renames` moves both `elmName` and
`capName`, so the row goes with the setter name: wc-dial's Attrs record grows
`readingNumeric` and has no `reading` field at all. That is what makes the crash
UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely avoided — the shared Probe.Attributes.reading is
the PROPERTY form (see _comment_controlled), and every element whose row carries
`reading` admits it, so scoping alone would still let a caller crash a wc-dial.
`attrTypes` is the other half and is not optional: without it the renamed setter is
still `String -> Attr`, which is the same lie under a new name. `float` matches the
`double` this element's IDL attribute actually is.

Output._comment: NB2f: <output>'s defaultValue is a property with no backing content attribute, so the default* companion must be SUPPRESSED here rather than emitting Ir.attribute "value".

Knob._comment: NB2g: opt one element back OUT of the brand roster. `pressed` then writes the content attribute, and gets no default* companion (that would be two setters for one fact).
